summary: N. R. Bhatt was an Indologist who held posts at the French Institute of Pondicherry and the École française d'Extrême-Orient, where he was attested as a member in 1966.

N. S. Ramachandra Murthy is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as an Epigraphy Assistant in the Department of Archaeology and Museums, Andhra Pradesh, and retired as Professor of Indian History and Archaeology at Sri Venkateswara University.

N. S. Ramanuja Tatacharya was an Indologist and philosopher. He worked as a researcher at the French Institute of Pondicherry around 1989 and served as Vice Chancellor of the National Sanskrit University from 1989 to 1994.
N. Taher is an archaeologist who succeeded K. K. Muhammed as the head of the Bhopal circle at the Archaeological Survey of India.

N. Veezhinathan, a scholar of Indology and philosophy, earned his PhD from Savitribai Phule Pune University in 1964 under A. Sankaran. He was a research scholar at Deccan College (1960–1963) and became Lecturer in Sanskrit at the University of Madras in 1964.

N. Venkataramanayya, a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology, studied under Ferrand E. Corley. He served as Reader in Indian History at the University of Madras (attested 1957) and Deputy Director for Epigraphy in the Andhra Pradesh Department of Archaeology and Museums.

Nadine Stchoupak was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Saint Petersburg State University and the École Pratique des Hautes Études. She served as Secretary and Librarian at the Institut de Civilisation Indienne (1927–1939) and taught Sanskrit at the EPHE (1931–1937).

Nae Ionescu was a philosopher and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Bucharest, the University of Göttingen, and the University of Munich. He held a post at the University of Bucharest from around 1920 to 1938.
Nagin J. Shah is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who succeeded Dalsukh Malvania and served as Acting Director at the L.D. Institute of Indology (attested 1968).

Nalinaksha Dutt was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who held doctorates from the University of Calcutta and the University of London. He was Professor of Pali at Judson College and Head of the Department of Pali at Calcutta University.

Nalini Balbir is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Colette Caillat. She held posts at the CNRS, Sorbonne Nouvelle University, and the École Pratique des Hautes Études, where she became Directeur d'Études in 2000 and Emerita Professor in 2022.

Nalini Devdas is a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. Supervised by Leslie Orr, she completed her PhD at Concordia University (attested 2004) and held a post at Carleton University.

Nam-lin Hur works in Japanology, religious studies, and history. After studying at the University of Tokyo and under Helen Hardacre, and completing a postdoctoral fellowship at Harvard University, he became professor of Japanese history and religious culture at the University of British Columbia.

Naman P. Ahuja is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who earned his doctorate from SOAS University of London. He is Professor of Indian Art and Architecture at Jawaharlal Nehru University (attested 2018).

Namgyal Rinpoche, active in Buddhist and religious studies, studied at the University of Michigan and Jarvis Baptist Seminary alongside various traditional teachers. He founded the Kagyu Samye Ling Monastery and Tibetan Centre in 1965 and the Dharma Centre of Canada in 1966.

Namio Egami was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (1927–1930), held a post there from 1931 to 1967, and directed the Ancient Orient Museum from around 1978 to 2002.
Namita Das is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed her PhD at Gauhati University under the supervision of Sibnath Sarma.

Namkhai Norbu was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at institutions including Derge Gonchen and Khamdre Shedra. He taught at Southwest Minzu University and served as Professor at the University of Naples 'L'Orientale' and University of Naples Federico II.

Nancy E. Levine is an anthropologist and Tibetologist who held posts at the University of California, Los Angeles, as Associate Professor of anthropology (attested 1998) and Professor of anthropology (attested 2026).

Nancy G. Lin is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology with degrees from Bryn Mawr College, Columbia University, UC Berkeley, and the University of Chicago. She has held posts at Lawrence University and the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research.
